title: Hoboing out of Virginia: Bluefield job and Zack Whyte's offer
summary: After Martinsville the stranded band took a Bluefield gig on a taxi debt; Zack Whyte offered to hire nine of them.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Listen. There's one story that... I suspect there's a story here. When the Blue Devils broke up... This is going way back. When the Blue Devils broke up, you had to hobo to St. Louis or something like that?
Yeah. We hoboed all the way to St. Louis.
Tell me about that. Because hoboing is pretty tough.
Yeah.
What exactly happened on that?

All right, I'll tell you what happened. We had left Martinsville, Virginia. A colored boy came over there, a youngster, he was about 25 years old -- 22 to 25, somewhere around there. Anyway, he said he had a big job for us. We wasn't doin' nothin' there in Martinsville. Just playing... Well, the doctor had a little old dance hall upstairs, up over his office. And he would give a dance up there on Saturday nights, up there, just for a little recreation and trying to make him a little money on the side, and maybe sometimes on a Sunday. Martinsville was a little small town anyhow, and the population was way down. There wasn't but a few colored people around there. But anyway, he'd make a little money up there, and he
Buster Smith - 204

would give... Down on the first floor next to his office, had a woman down there running a restaurant. So he would tell her to feed us all the week, until we played the weekend, and then he'd give us some money. In other words, he's just paying the expense.

So this boy... We didn't have no transportation, no cars. One broke down, and then when we got ready, the man come to take them and all that kind of stuff. So we were stranded there. We couldn't get out, and it's (?) right in the spring.

So when this boy come and got us, said he had a job over at Bluefield, West Virginia. And we got two taxicab drivers, colored taxicab drivers. They wanted seventy dollars. They took us over there. The boy said we could go over there and we had a week to work. And we're going to make good money out of it. All right, we got the taxicab drivers to carry us over there. Didn't give them a quarter.
We got there, went out there and played for White folks. Went out and played, and the hall was just about as big as this house...
Tiny.

Yeah. You could get about 25 or 30 people in there, and we have a big 13-piece band sitting up there playing, and this little small bunch of people there. We seen wasn't nothin' goin' to happen there, but we had to stay there. We
Buster Smith - 205

played about three nights. So Zach Whyte heard that we... He had a big band in Cincinnati, and he heard that we was down there in this town, playing there. And he needed nine men in his band. I think his band had broke up or something, and he wanted nine of us. We were going to go with it, but he didn't want the whole band; he just wanted nine of us.
Who did he want to leave behind?
He wanted to leave the trombone player...
That's Drew (?).

Yeah, Drew (?). He wanted to leave the drummer, Raymond Howell. And he wanted to leave I think the other trombone player, Jap Allen...no, Jap Jones -- they wanted to leave him. And I think he wanted Leroy White, ...(?)... in Des Moines.
He wanted Leroy White.

Yeah, he wanted him. Anyway, he wanted nine out of the band. Mostly he wanted the reed section and some of the trumpets. He wanted George Hudson -- he was the only trumpet. And I think Milton Thomas(?). We had three trumpet players.
